title: PRD: Tiered response guarantees, error-burn modeling, and canary escalation flow for streaming API
creator: Ava Patel
description: Define a pragmatic PRD that establishes tiered latency and availability guarantees for Redwood's streaming text API, a transparent error-budget burn model per tenant tier, and an automated canary escalation flow usable by Hosted and Dedicated customers. Deliverables: SLO matrix, burn-rate formulas, rollout gating rules, console indicators for canary health, and CI contract tests for model upgrades.
background: Customers using streaming endpoints are sensitive to first-token latency, sustained per-token throughput, and tail latency spikes during traffic shifts. Recent incidents exposed gaps in our canary escalation (slow detection, manual rollbacks) and inconsistent communication of error-budget status to customer success. This PRD consolidates learnings and creates enforceable gates for safe progressive rollouts of model or runtime changes affecting streaming behavior.
scope_changes: Initial scope limited to streaming text/generation API (not embeddings or vector-updates)
Applies to Hosted + Dedicated; Private (VPC) will be a follow-up to align on telemetry access
Does not include automatic cross-region failover in this phase; that is a separate project
requirements: Define three tenant tiers (Basic, Standard, Enterprise) with explicit latency/availability targets for first-token and sustained token generation
Specify burn-rate formula and sliding window semantics for error-budget depletion (minute-level and hourly-level windows)
Design a canary escalation flow that includes automated mitigation steps (traffic throttling, model fallback to 'compat' variant, alerting) and clear thresholds for human intervention
Add console visibility: per-canary health indicator, remaining error-budget percentage, and recent tail-latency spikes
Create CI contract tests that validate SLO adherence for any runtime or model change before canary rollout
acceptance_criteria: SLO matrix drafted and reviewed by Eng, SRE, and Sales Engineering and merged into PRD doc
Burn-rate model implemented in metrics pipeline and validated against two historical incidents with reproducible calculations
Canary escalation flow documented and automated in the rollout runner so that 95% of canaries reach automated mitigation within 30s of threshold breach
Console surfaces per-canary health with a single-click abort for on-call and product owners
CI contract test added to monorepo and blocks canary rollout when the simulated baseline exceeds SLOs in synthetic workloads
rollout_gates: Gate A (smoke): Basic functional checks + first-token median not worse than baseline+25%
Gate B (early canary): P95 first-token latency <= tier threshold and no error-budget burn > 0.5% in 10m sliding window
Gate C (progressive ramp): cumulative burn-rate < 0.75 over 30m and tail error rate < 0.5% for Standard/Enterprise
Gate D (full rollout): remaining error-budget >= 30% for Basic and >= 60% for Enterprise, otherwise require manual approval
metrics: Per-token throughput (tokens/sec) distribution by request size
Error rate (5xx + model-timeout) by tenant and canary
dependencies: ENG-20187: Streaming telemetry retention increase on metrics pipeline
ENG-21045: Canary runner support for automatic model fallback
ENG-21411: Console canary widget and abort action

notes: Trade-offs discussed: tighter SLOs increase false positives during noisy network conditions; mitigation is configurable sensitivity per-customer in Enterprise tier.
Fallback model variants should be explicitly labeled 'compat' and have separate perf profiles to avoid rollback loop.
We will ramp observability retention to 7 days for canary-specific windows to support post-hoc analysis (ENG-20187).
